# Ternent libraries

> TypeScript ESM libraries for portable signed history, encrypted application documents,
> identity capabilities and standalone proofs. This is the consumer entry point for agents.

## Choose the interface

- [Concord](packages/concord/llms.txt): build an application using typed commands, events, authority, private groups and replay.
- [Ledger](packages/ledger/llms.txt): build a standalone signed log without Concord application or permission semantics.
- [Identity](packages/identity/llms.txt): create, back up, restore or recover one identity; sign and verify bytes.
- [Armour](packages/armour/llms.txt): encrypt/decrypt with age; compose identity capabilities and explicit Ledger payload codecs.
- [Seal](packages/seal/llms.txt): sign and verify a detached proof over any bytes' hash; use the Node CLI.

The active libraries are exactly the five above. Workspace and UI are outside this
release, and Utils and separate Seal CLI packages are retired. Use the published
exports rather than historical workspace runtime/plugin examples.

## Installation and source of truth

Each package guide names its stable interface version. Check npm availability
before installing from an unreleased checkout, and commit the consumer lockfile.

Install only the libraries the application uses. An unqualified package install selects
npm's `latest` tag; `@next` selects the preview channel. Dist-tags and version stability
are separate: check the resolved version, including any prerelease suffix, in the
consumer lockfile. Libraries support Node 22.18+ and modern browsers; Seal’s CLI
and filesystem operations require Node. Core development uses its own pinned toolchain.

The package guides link to their public README and declarations. The published
`dist/*.d.ts` files define the installed interface; do not infer APIs from old examples
or import repository source. Package READMEs and these guides are included in this
checkout’s package file lists.

Already published tarballs are immutable; moving a dist-tag does not add files to
them. Older releases may predate these guides. Match the repository guide to the
installed package's declarations when its tarball has no guide.

## Shared contracts

Signed committed history is authoritative; projections are derived. Local commits and
storage publication are separate. Staged Ledger entries and Concord drafts stay in
memory. Private identity capabilities are held outside the document; the host owns
identity persistence, recovery and synchronization.

Use the owning library's verification and cryptography rather than implementing them
in the application. Documents never load executable code: hosts select trusted models
and system implementations. Treat inspection evidence separately from trusted state.

Snapshots have one selected head. Compare equal/ahead/behind/diverged/unrelated; never
silently choose or combine divergent history. A storage adapter may implement atomic
expected-head publication. After an explicit rejected write, retain local bytes and
command intents, reopen the accepted snapshot and reissue the intended command under
current authority. Reissue can fail validation; retain the work for resolution. This
is host behavior, not an automatic retry or merge method in Concord. No runtime
`merge`, `push`, `pull`, checkpoint, draft persistence or model-upgrade API exists.

- [Protocol](docs/concord/alpha-protocol.md): specialist wire, signatures and canonicalization.
- [Contributor instructions](AGENTS.md): repository maintenance rather than application usage.
